structure.overview: The Minister of Citizenship and Immigration sought judicial review of the Immigration Appeal Division's (IAD) decision allowing Mr. Doss's appeal of a visa refusal for his mother based on excessive health-related demand. Mr. Doss, the applicant, argued that his mother's health condition was stable and that humanitarian and compassionate (H&C) grounds justified the appeal, while the Minister, the respondent, contended the IAD erred in its assessment of health and H&C factors. The Federal Court allowed the Minister's application for judicial review, finding the IAD's decision unreasonable and setting it aside for reconsideration.

party_points.text: IAD erred in finding stable health and assessing H&C grounds
Mother's health stable, improved kidney condition, H&C grounds including insecurity in Egypt

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The Minister seeks judicial review of the IAD decision allowing Mr. Doss's appeal of a visa refusal for his mother.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court allows the application for judicial review.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: Mr. Doss, a Canadian citizen born in Egypt, seeks to sponsor his mother, a Spanish citizen living in Egypt, aged 81 and widowed.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: An immigration officer refused the sponsorship due to Ms. Finianos's health condition causing excessive demand under IRPA s 38(1).

citations.cite: Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, SC 2001, c 27

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The officer relied on IRCC physician's opinion about costly dialysis and transplant needs, noting public funding and long waiting lists.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: Mr. Doss appealed, alleging stable health, improved kidney condition, transplant not recommended over 80, and H&C grounds including insecurity in Egypt.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: IRCC medical team requested a new medical exam to reassess the officer's decision after Mr. Doss's appeal.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The IAD hearing was held on August 5, 2020, with Mr. Doss as the sole witness.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The IAD allowed the appeal but found the nephrologist's report irrelevant and upheld the 2017 and 2019 medical results showing excessive demand risk.
idea_list: medical results valid showing excessive demand

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The IAD found illness costs significant but temporary, noting Ms. Finianos's age and limited short-term health service needs.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The IAD gave significant weight to Mr. Doss's close relationship and financial ability to care for his mother.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The IAD found Ms. Finianos had little support in Egypt and that living with other children abroad was unrealistic, favoring Mr. Doss's support.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The IAD concluded sufficient H&C considerations offset the excessive demand on health services under IRPA objectives.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The Minister argues the IAD erred in finding stable health and in assessing H&C grounds against the seriousness of diagnosis and costs.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The applicable standard of review for IAD decisions under IRPA s 67(1)(c) is reasonableness, citing Vavilov and Khosa.

citations.cite: Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v Vavilov, 2019 SCC 65 at paras 10, 16–17
citations.why: States reasonableness standard for IAD decisions

citations.cite: Canada (Citizenship and Immigration) v Khosa, 2009 SCC 12 at para 58
citations.why: Confirms reasonableness standard for IAD decisions

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Under reasonableness, the court reviews the decision's justification, transparency, intelligibility, and rationality per Vavilov.

citations.why: Explains reasonableness review criteria and burden

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court accepts the Minister's argument that the IAD's findings on illness cost burden lack coherent and rational analysis.

citations.why: Supports finding of incoherent and irrational analysis

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: IRPA s 38(1) defines inadmissibility on health grounds for excessive demand; 'excessive demand' is defined in IRPR s 1(1).

citations.cite: Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, SC 2001, c 27 s 38(1)
Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, SOR/2002-227 s 1(1)

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: Sponsorship refusals on health grounds can be appealed to the IAD under IRPA ss 63(1) and 67(1)(c) for H&C special relief.

citations.cite: Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, SC 2001, c 27 ss 63(1), 67(1)(c)

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Jugpall establishes that H&C grounds must match the seriousness of inadmissibility; more serious cases require stronger H&C.

citations.cite: Jugpall v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), [1999] IADD No 600 (QL)
citations.why: Explains proportionality of H&C grounds to inadmissibility

citations.cite: Patel v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2019 FC 394

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The IAD relied on IRCC physicians' findings of excessive demand, as no other medical results were available.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The IAD found Ms. Finianos's condition stable and short-term care needs limited, based on Mr. Doss's testimony.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court finds the IAD's short-term care duration finding unsupported by medical prognosis, including transplant timing.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Mr. Doss argues kidney transplants are unrealistic over age 80, relying on a scientific article and statistical charts.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court finds Mr. Doss's evidence outdated, lacking context, and inconsistent with the IRCC physician's opinion.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Mr. Doss presented little evidence to undermine diagnosis; his testimony is hearsay and Ms. Finianos refused full exams.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court defers to IAD but finds its inconsistent analysis may have caused error in balancing H&C and family reunification.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The IAD decision lacks reasonableness; the court allows review, sets aside decision, and refers for reconsideration.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: No question of general importance was certified or arises in this case.
